addressee_block:
The Labour Commissioner
[District/State] Labour Department
[Office Address]
relevant_acts: Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (in force nationally from 21 November 2025 — for disputes/events on or after that date)
Code on Wages, 2019 (in force nationally from 21 November 2025 — supersedes the Payment of Wages Act 1936 and Minimum Wages Act 1948 for events on or after that date)
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 / Payment of Wages Act, 1936 / Minimum Wages Act, 1948 (only for events before 21 November 2025)
institution_rules: Clearly state the employer-employee relationship (designation, dates of employment, wages agreed), the specific grievance (unpaid wages, wrongful termination, non-payment of statutory dues, etc.), and the amount claimed. Attach the appointment letter, salary slips, termination notice/order (if any), and any prior correspondence with the employer. Wage-recovery claims are ordinarily filed before the Payment of Wages Authority (now the wage-claim authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, for post-21-November-2025 events); industrial disputes over termination or conditions of service ordinarily require conciliation before the Labour Officer/Commissioner before adjudication. For events/disputes on or after 21 November 2025, cite the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and Code on Wages, 2019 as the governing law, NOT the repealed Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Payment of Wages Act 1936, or Minimum Wages Act 1948. For events before that date, cite the older Acts instead. State-specific rules under the new Codes were still rolling out shortly after the 21 November 2025 notification, so use [VERIFY: state-specific rules under the Industrial Relations Code/Code on Wages] if the applicable State's rules are uncertain. NEVER invent a case or reference number. For offences and procedures after 1 July 2024, cite the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) — NOT the repealed IPC 1860, CrPC 1973, or Indian Evidence Act 1872. The Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and RTI Act 2005 remain in force and may be cited. If unsure of a new-code section number, use [VERIFY].
